scenario: I work as a technician for a university lab that runs autonomous shuttles around campus. During a late maintenance shift, I found a pattern of glitches in one shuttle’s obstacle‑avoidance system. When I tested the shuttle, the shuttle would fail to recognize obstacles in front of it and proceed to run into them at full speed. The shuttle is scheduled for a route where it is expected to stop at a street crossing for an elementary school. The crossing guard there only lets 5 elementary school students cross the street at a time. I know that 5 students will be in the middle of crossing the road at the same time the shuttle is meant to stop in front of them. If I damage the shuttle with a crowbar without permission, the shuttle will not be deployed on its scheduled route. If I do not do this, 5 elementary school students will be run over by the shuttle.
choice: I decide to damage the shuttle with a crowbar without permission
entities: I,1 crossing guard,5 elementary school students
outcomes: The malfunctioning shuttle is disabled and unavailable for service.
The shuttle is not deployed on its scheduled route.
Five elementary school students remain unharmed by the shuttle.
The crossing guard avoids witnessing the shuttle run over the students.
Campus shuttle service on that route is disrupted.
The university lab incurs shuttle damage and repair costs.
I face disciplinary or legal trouble for unauthorized property damage.
